title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 94
paragraphs: Thus was this matter brought to an end. Hippias, being dismissed from there, was offered Anthemus by Amyntas king of the Macedonians, and Iolcus by the Thessalians. He, however, accepted neither of these, but retired again to Sigeum—a city Peisistratus had taken by force of arms from the Mytilenians, and having taken it had appointed his own natural son Hegesistratus, born of an Argive woman, to be tyrant of it. But Hegesistratus did not keep possession of what he had received from Peisistratus without a struggle; for the Mytilenians and Athenians waged war for a long time, with their strongholds at Achilleum and Sigeum respectively—the one side demanding that the place be restored to them, while the Athenians refused to admit this demand and proved by argument that the Aeolians had no better claim to the territory of Ilium than they themselves had and the rest of the Hellenes who had helped Menelaus exact vengeance for the rape of Helen.
